# Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 68 (Bi-Vb Pc68)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 68 (*Sahajīvinī-ananuggahaṇa*) is a monastic rule in the Theravāda Vinaya governing the conduct of Buddhist nuns (*bhikkhunīs*), specifically regarding their responsibilities toward newly ordained students. According to the rule, a nun who ordains a student (*sahajīvinī*) but fails to guide and support her (*anugaṇheyya* / *anugaṇhāpeyya*) for two years commits an offense requiring confession (*pācittiya*) [Bechert et al. 1997]. In the Vinaya narrative framework, the transgressing nun is exemplified by Thullanandā acting as the preceptor (*upajjhā*) [Hüsken 1997]. The commentary and word analysis explain that the designation *sahajīvinī* refers to a newly ordained nun living in dependence upon her mentor [Hüsken 1997]. Scholars note that this obligation of support over two years parallels the *sammāvattanā* duties of a preceptor found in the Khandhakas, which include caring for and nursing the co-resident in times of illness, thereby linking the scope of this rule with Bhikkhunī Pācittiya 34 [Bechert et al. 1997].

Full parallels are preserved in the Pātimokkha and Parivāra of the Pali tradition, as well as in the Vinayas of other early Buddhist schools preserved in Chinese and Tibetan translations, including the Mahīśāsaka (*Lzh Mi Bi Vb Pc112*) and Mūlasarvāstivāda (*Lzh Mu Bi Vb Pc 114*; Tibetan *xct-mu-bi-vb-pc90*) traditions. Related or resembling rules on failing to support or instruct a co-resident occur in the Dharmaguptaka, Sarvāstivāda, Mahāsāṅghika, and Mahāsāṅghika-Lokottaravāda traditions, as well as the closely linked Theravāda rule Bhikkhunī Pācittiya 70. DharmaNexus identifies extensive Pali-internal textual reuse across the Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga, most heavily with Pācittiyas 69, 70, and 34, while also showing cross-language alignments with the Sanskrit *Bhikṣuṇīvinaya* and Tibetan commentaries such as the *Vinayasūtravṛtti* and the *Āryasarvāstivādimūlabhikṣuṇīpratimokṣasūtravṛtti* [DharmaNexus].
